body:
`scripts/preflight-release-tag.sh` (autopilot workspace, outside this repo)
carries four release-bookkeeping checks, including check #3, which compares the
`VERSION` file at the target commit against the version being tagged.

Run against the real tag it refuses correctly:

    $ bash scripts/preflight-release-tag.sh v4.1.32 v4.1.32
    REFUSING to tag v4.1.32 at 313982f58 (v4.1.32) -- release bookkeeping incomplete:
      - VERSION reads '4.1.31' at v4.1.32, expected '4.1.32'
    exit=1

The script was committed 2026-08-06T14:37Z, about 18 hours BEFORE the v4.1.32
tag (2026-08-07T08:31:45Z). So the gate existed, was correct, was available, and
the defective release shipped anyway — because nothing invokes it. Its only
caller in the tree is a sentence of prose, LOOP.md:176 ("Gate before tagging:
... must pass"). The release tick cuts the tag directly with
`gh release create --target <sha>` and never runs it.

This is the wedge-audit shape: the question is not only "does the gate heal or
signal" but "can the gate be skipped by omission". A gate whose invocation
depends on a model remembering a prose instruction is documentation.

#1437 is fixed at a different layer on purpose: `tests/unit/
test_1437_version_matches_changelog.py` pins VERSION against the newest dated
CHANGELOG release section, so the drift goes red in CI on the pre-tag
bookkeeping PR — upstream of the tag, which is the last point where a fix is
still free. That closes the VERSION hole specifically.

The other three preflight checks (changelog section present, [Unreleased]
drained, whatsNew entry) remain enforced only by prose. Remaining work: either
give the release path a single scripted entry point that runs preflight before
`gh release create`, or mirror each surviving check into repo-side CI the way
the VERSION one now is. Prefer the latter where the artifact is in-tree — CI
cannot be skipped by omission.
title: preflight-release-tag.sh is a correct gate with no caller — invocation depends on prose in LOOP.md
